Maya (oncall): handoff — evening -> night. I'm primary for the next 8h, Aj is secondary. Quick summary: embedding-autoscaler oscillation triggered repeated cold starts and transient 503s for our embeddings endpoint around 20:12 UTC. We applied a temporary mitigation (pin autoscaler min_replicas=2 and disabled burst policy) and added a routing rule to drain traffic to the fallback cpu-pool for small requests. No open customer pages at this time, but Support saw a handful of support tickets for slow/failed embeddings. See dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/embeds/autoscale and https://slo.redwood/embeddings/availability

Aj Patel: thanks — saw the incident-bot alerts. Do we have exact window and error counts? I want to correlate with deploys.

Maya (oncall): incident-bot posted: "INCIDENT: embeddings-autoscaler-thrash — pages: 3 — status: mitigated (temporary)" at 1815005000. Error spike from 20:11:30 -> 20:18:40 UTC. ~420 5xx responses total across all regions, peak p95 latency for embeddings jumped to 2.3s. No deploys during that window (checked deploy-bot).

Sophia (SRE): logs look like the autoscaler overreacted to a short burst of long-lived inference workers. Scaling down too aggressively caused cold start penalty on large models. I pulled a snippet from the autoscaler logs:

```
2026-03-15T20:11:31Z autoscaler: scale_down_decision: delta_load=-0.45 threshold=0.2
2026-03-15T20:11:32Z autoscaler: terminating pod embed-worker-7f9c
2026-03-15T20:11:33Z embed-service: pod_startup_time=6.8s kernel_init=1.1s model_load=4.5s
```

Sophia (SRE): TL;DR: scale down thresholds too tight for embedding model cold-start time. Suggest change: introduce cooldown window and increase min_replicas for embeddings workload.

Jordan (support): customers impacted were 3 small teams (non-enterprise). I flagged them in support queue and offered temporary retry guidance. No refunds requested. Slack threads: https://support.redwood/tickets/INC-1234

Luca (eng-lead): good call on routing to cpu-pool. Any risk to capacity there? We should confirm that fallback doesn't increase tail latency for CPU-backed requests.

Maya (oncall): CPU-pool has spare headroom right now; routing rule only sends requests with payload_size < 512 tokens to cpu-fallback. Config applied via operations console. Rule snippet:

```
route: embeddings
condition: request.payload_tokens <= 512
action: route_to: cpu-fallback
```

Maya (oncall): current status: mitigated (temporary). Autoscaler pinned to min_replicas=2 across regions, burst policy disabled. Error rates falling back to baseline since 20:22 UTC. Monitoring set to 1m alerting. I've created a short-lived dashboard panel and alerted Sophia.

Aj Patel: action items? I'll take follow-up on autoscaler config and a safer scale-down heuristic. Will create a PR for config + unit tests.

Sophia (SRE): I'll draft a runbook amendment for embedding autoscaler: add a cooldown of 3m after scale-down, require model-load <= 3s or else bump min_replicas automatically. Also add a health-probe that preloads model weights in background. Putting link to runbook draft: https://playbooks.redwood/embeds-autoscaler-draft

Maya (oncall): I'm adding the oncall tickets: "+1 follow-up: autoscaler config PR (Aj) | +1 runbook update (Sophia) | +1 support followup to customers (Jordan)."

ops-bot: "Scheduled job: create post-incident snapshot at 22:00 UTC — snapshot_id=sn-20260315-2200"

incident-bot: "INCIDENT UPDATE: embeddings-autoscaler-thrash — status: mitigated — severity: P2 — pager cleared at 20:26 UTC — incident_ref: INC-20260315-07"

Jordan (support): I'll reply to the affected customers with a summary and ETA for fix. Tagging support playbook: #support-embeddings

Maya (oncall): Next steps for night shift (Aj -> primary at 23:00 UTC if I don't close):
- Aj: review autoscaler telemetry, open PR for config changes, run load test against staging with new heuristic
- Sophia: finalize runbook updates and add unit test harness for cold-start detection
- Jordan: confirm customer notifications closed and mark any follow-ups
- Maya: handover docs + attach logs to incident ticket

Aj Patel: ack. I'll start with reproducer against staging and post results here. If I can't get repro by 02:00 UTC, escalate to Luca.

Maya (oncall): FYI — created incident ticket INC-20260315-07 with summary and attached logs. I'll add a short postmortem template and invite Luca, Sophia, Aj.

Luca (eng-lead): please include cost impact estimate and which customers were affected. We'll decide btw whether this is a postmortem or a blameless incident review.

Maya (oncall): added cost estimates and customer list to ticket. Closing notes: mitigated for night; handing to Aj at 23:00 UTC unless he requests takeover earlier. If anything spikes again, page the usual oncall channel and call the oncall bridge.

Aj Patel: thanks. Leaving a note w/ my pager duty number and escalation policy. Will post a short summary after initial triage.

Maya (oncall): handoff complete. :white_check_mark: Good luck, team.
